answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identities to physical unclonable functions on microchips no larger than a walnut. Whether monitoring a cedar grove or a juniper ridge, each agent authenticates via challenge responses from unforgeable silicon variations. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware expense of purchasing distinct physical chips per clone. However, thermal drift is a key limitation, as temperature swings alter circuit delays and induce false rejections.
